chapter: Sanger, Ben Black and carnival balls
title: Calling the band back with a D minor chord and giving away batons
summary: He explains tuning up as a signal for the band, giving away batons, and handling critical customers.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Papaya, to the contrary, wants to stress that he plays a lot of carnival balls. He brings up a lot of people with carnival costumes on and it's a motley mess with people falling all over and sitting in front of the band and look like a... Oh, no. I went for the artistic. But the only thing is, every time I want to get a ticket, test somebody was doing something else.
Well I said, the hell with you, I'm going to tune up. Hit the D minor chord, we're going to tune it again. I want that A, don't you want the A before you go on the air?

Oh yeah. I was the only band in town that never had to look around for musicians. When I picked the A kind of, the D minor chord on the piano, my band knew that's the time to come back on the bandstand. And nobody knew I was calling them. Because they thought I was tuning up, see. I go, and if they didn't come right away, they hit it hard, then they come, see. Because they had intermission, I didn't stop telling where they'd go, they'd see their friends, they'd go get a drink, a cup of coffee. But when they heard the D minor chord, they'd come back on. And I thought that was a good deal, don't you think? Oh yeah. I also had another deal that I cut it out. I got a lot of cheap batons with my name on it. And I used to accidentally lose them, you know, let them go. And the kids used to scramble for me. I thought it was a gag, don't you think so? Oh sure. I'm sure it worked for you. I said, I put on a merry Christmas, you've got to get drunk. All that helps. But you can't please everybody. You're playing for, a man will come up and give you a job, he's wanting to hire you for years, like Loyola alumni. He's 55, 60 years old. He knows Margie and high society and stuff like that. And he wants it. He gave you the engagement. You play it and some young punks, they want to put you down, you know? They want that job. They're even dancing. I said, you don't dance, you don't move. What are you complaining about? They're standing on one spot. They said, you know, can't you play some decent music? I would punch him in the nose. If I'd have been a big guy there'd have been a lot of broken noses around this town. I'd say they did fool with Blue Steel. You ever hear of Blue Steel?
